query: Earlier W-based high-entropy alloys showed promising microstructural stability, high-temperature strength, and irradiation tolerance, but most contained Nb, Mo, Cr, or Ni, whose activation behavior and other service limitations restrict their suitability for plasma-facing components. Candidate structural materials must combine thermal and mechanical performance with low neutron activation and rapid radioactive decay. The equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy uses refractory, relatively low-activation constituents and has shown creep and molten-salt-corrosion resistance, yet its plastic strain and toughness remain unreported and poorly understood. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains what governs its plastic strain and toughness relative to commercially used pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service? Specify a controlled comparison that would isolate the hypothesized cause, the observations predicted relative to pure tungsten, the boundaries of validity, the cited prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an observation that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The plastic strain and toughness of the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy are governed by its grain boundary cohesion and the formation of nanometer-scale bubbles under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service.
generation.conditions: Exposure to large plasma heat and an intense mixture of ionized and energetic neutral species of hydrogen isotopes (D and T), He ash, and neutrons
generation.mechanism: Formation of nanometer-scale bubbles and dislocation nucleation and movement
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved plastic strain and toughness compared to commercially used pure tungsten
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanisms of grain boundary cohesion and bubble formation under high-temperature service conditions are not well understood

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy and pure tungsten under high-temperature plasma-facing-component service conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the equimolar WTaTiVZr alloy does not exhibit improved plastic strain and toughness compared to pure tungsten under high-temperature service conditions, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text: Key components in magnetic fusion reactors, such as the divertor or the plasma-facing materials (PFMs), are required to have stringent properties including low activation, high melting point, good thermomechanical properties, low sputter erosion, and low tritium retention/codeposition. They must operate at high temperature (≥1000 K) for long durations (>10 7 s), without failure or extensive erosion while exposed to large plasma heat and an intense mixture of ionized and energetic neutral species of hydrogen isotopes (D and T), He ash (fluxes, >10 24 m −2 s −1 ), and neutrons ( [1] ). Tungsten (W) is the leading PFM candidate because of its high melting temperature, low erosion rates, and small tritium retention. These advantages are unfortunately coupled with very low fracture toughness characterized by brittle transgranular and intergranular failure regimes, which severely restrict the useful operating temperature window and also create a range of fabrication difficulties. Furthermore, blistering at moderate temperature (<800 K) by D and He ( [2] , [3] ) and the formation of pits, holes, and bubbles by He at higher temperature (>1600 K) ( [4] ) have all been observed. One of the most promising and progressive fields in modern material science is high-entropy alloys (HEAs). The first to propose HEAs’ concept was J.W. Yeh [ [1] ], but since then, it has changed rather significantly, especially during the last few years [ [2] ]. Due to their extremely high mechanical and physical properties, refractory HEAs are classified as a separate group of materials. Such alloying compositions mainly include elements from the IV, V, and VI columns of the periodic table with some additions of Al, Si, Ni, or Co [ [3] ].

First high-entropy equiatomic compositions based on refractory elements, such as NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWV, were obtained in prior research [ [4] , [5] ]. It was found that the alloys possess higher mechanical properties at higher temperatures in comparison to conventional superalloys, such as Inconel 718 and Haynes 230 [ [6] ]. It was also determined that the addition of V increases the hardness significantly (up to 11.4 GPa at 1150 °C) [ [7] ] and yield strength σ 0.2 from 1058 MPa to 1246 MPa [ [5] ].
